To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mTORC1 and mTORC2 signaling is increased upon loss of NF2, a tumor suppressor in NF2-deficient arachnoid cells and meningioma cells.

mTORC1 and mTORC2 inhibition downregulate neuregulin signaling and upregulate insulin receptor signaling and that combined inhibition of mTORC1, mTORC2, and insulin receptor may be an effective strategy to treat NF2-deficient tumors.

mTORC1 and mTORC2 inhibition disrupts neugregulin-1/ERBB3 autocrine signaling in NF2-deficient human meningioma cells, leading to activation of insulin receptor substrate 1 (IRS1) and insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF1) signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new technologies and methods for the treatment of meningiomas.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies to target meningiomas.
understanding the molecular pathways that lead to the development of meningiomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mTOR pathway is an important therapeutic target in meningiomas, especially those with NF2 loss.

our data indicate that mTORC1 and 2 inhibition disrupts NRG1-EPHB3 autocrine signaling, which leads to increased pAkt T308 activation through an adaptive response that involves upregulation of the insulin receptor (INSR).
the mTOR kinase inhibitors, AZD8055 and Torin1, downregulate neuregulin (NRGI) secretion and activation of the ERBB3 receptor kinase in NF2-null cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NF2-deficient tumors are dependent on mTORC1 and mTORC2 signaling and that mTOR inhibition sensitizes these cells to other therapies.
NF2-deficient AC and MN cells show increased NRG1 expression/secretion, which activates ERBB3, and mTOR kinase inhibition disrupt the NRG1– ERBB3 autocrine loop, leading to increased pAkt T308.
mTOR kinase inhibition disrupt neuregulin1–ERBB signaling and sensitizes meningiomas to IGF1/insulin receptor kinase inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we identified a novel signaling mechanism in NF2-deficient arachnoid cells, specifically the activation of NRG1/ERBB3 signaling, which can be targeted by mTORC1 inhibition and IGF1/insulin receptor inhibition.
NF2 loss activates mTOR signaling and leads to adaptive changes in cellular signaling that can be exploited for treatment of NF-2-deficient meningiom.
NF2-deficient tumors are sensitive to mTORC1 inhibition.
